title: Copilot Studio: discover and add skills from the skills catalog
summary: Hold: the maker sharing path starts at an agent's Build tab without telling readers how to reach that agent. The roadmap facts, package-management operations and qualified billing statements are supported; the availability API example also needs a minor formatting correction.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns discovering and adding skills in Microsoft Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Discover & Add Skills from the skill catalog

claims.claim: The planned catalog lets makers discover approved organisational skills.
claims.quote: With the Skills catalog in Copilot Studio, makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills

claims.claim: Makers can reuse skills instead of recreating instructions and workflows for every agent.
claims.quote: instead of recreating the same instructions and workflows for every agent

claims.claim: The planned catalog supports selectively sharing approved organisational skills.
claims.quote: makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store.
claims.quote: The shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store

claims.claim: The roadmap says shared skills can extend across Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.
claims.quote: enables shared skills to extend across experiences such as Copilot Studio M365 copilot, and Cowork

claims.claim: The roadmap describes centralised governance for the shared catalog.
claims.quote: helping organizations standardize proven ways of working while maintaining centralized governance

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the roadmap's Copilot Studio skills catalog by that name.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "Browse skills" "catalog"; opened skills-manage, skills-overview, skills-add-existing and Package Management API overview. None identifies the roadmap catalog.

claims.claim: Learn does not state whether Browse skills is the same catalog as the roadmap's.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "Browse skills" "catalog"; opened skills-manage and skills-overview. They describe browsing shared skills without identifying roadmap item 571880 or its App Store catalog.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Within an open agent, makers select Build, the plus icon next to Skills, Browse skills (preview), a skill and Add.
claims.quote: Open your agent in Copilot Studio. ... Select the Build tab. ... Select the + icon next to Skills, and then select Browse skills (preview). ... Select the skill you want to add. ... On the skill details page, select Add.

claims.claim: The skills available in Browse skills are those shared by admins or skill owners.
claims.quote: The skills available to you are the ones shared by admins or skill owners.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A skill is defined by a name, description and instructions that guide the agent on a task.
claims.quote: A skill is a capability defined by a name, a description, and instructions that tell the agent how to handle specific types of tasks or scenarios.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding a shared skill gives the agent a snapshot that retains a reference to the original.
claims.quote: When you add a shared skill, the agent gets a snapshot of the skill while maintaining a reference to the original shared skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Makers receive an update notification when opening an agent that uses an older shared-skill version.
claims.quote: You receive a skill update notification when you open an agent that uses an older version of a shared skill.

claims.claim: Makers can choose to update an older shared skill.
claims.quote: You can choose to update to the new version by selecting the update button for the skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: A maker can share a skill they created and choose its audience.
claims.quote: When you share a skill you created, you and other people in your organization can use it in their Copilot Studio agents. You can keep the skill private or share it with specific people or groups in your organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The sharing options are Only you and Specific users or groups in your organization.
claims.quote: Only you: Keeps the skill private to your account. ... Specific users or groups in your organization: Lets you add people or groups by name or email address.

claims.claim: People and groups a skill is shared with can add it to their agents.
claims.quote: The people and groups you share with can then add the skill to their agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An edited shared skill must be shared again to make its latest version available to recipients.
claims.quote: When you edit and change a skill that you already shared, share the skill again to make the latest version available to those you previously shared it with.

claims.claim: A skill package can include supporting scripts, templates and reference documents.
claims.quote: The package can optionally include supporting files, such as scripts, templates, and reference documents.

claims.claim: The runtime decides to activate skills from the user's request and the skill description, without requiring the user to name the skill.
claims.quote: The orchestration runtime decides when to activate a skill based on the user's message and the skill's description.

claims.claim: A skill can instruct an agent to use a specific tool.
claims.quote: For example, a skill might instruct your agent to use a specific tool in a particular way.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The documented browse and sharing flows are preview and subject to change.
claims.quote: Browse and add shared skills (preview) ... Share a skill (preview) ... This article contains Microsoft Copilot Studio preview documentation and is subject to change.

claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: a maker chooses to browse and add a skill, and no catalog-specific enablement switch was found.
claims.quote: On the skill details page, select Add. Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles catalog; opened skills-manage and skills-copilot-studio-rule. No Browse skills enablement switch was stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated an arrival-time administrative action for the roadmap catalog.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles catalog; opened skills-manage, skills-overview and skills-copilot-studio-rule; read roadmap record. No catalog rollout action or default-arrival notice was found.

claims.claim: No setting specifically governing or disabling Browse skills or the roadmap catalog is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles catalog; opened skills-manage and skills-copilot-studio-rule. The latter documents a general skills rule but does not identify Browse skills or the catalog.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-level switch specifically restricting maker sharing of these shared skills is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skills sharing API tenant control approval catalog; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "skills" "sharing" "administrator" "harness". Opened skills-manage and skills-copilot-studio-rule; no such switch found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an additional approval step for a maker adding a shared skill.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skills sharing API tenant control approval catalog; opened skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers. The shared-skill flow ends with Add; no additional approval step is stated for that flow.

claims.claim: The Learn shared-skill page does not specify what organisational data a catalog skill can reach.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog Microsoft 365 registry package governance harness data access; opened skills-manage, skills-overview and skills-add-existing. No catalog-specific data-access boundaries are stated.

claims.claim: Consumption is the documented billing model used for the harness discussed in this briefing.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness ... use a usage-based billing structure.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The skills documentation warns that using, building, testing and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness credit charging starts when building starts.
claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.claim: Variable cost is supported by a usage meter measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licence specific to the skills catalog is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog license price credits browsing adding sharing; opened skills-manage, billing-credit-overview and Package Management API overview; read licensing search excerpts. No catalog-specific licence is named.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No catalog-specific rate or charge for browsing, adding or sharing a skill is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog license price credits browsing adding sharing; opened skills-manage, skills-add-existing and billing-credit-overview; read Billing rates and management excerpts. No catalog-operation rate is stated.

claims.claim: Using a shared skill does not take an agent outside its documented harness billing.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself. Any experience that uses one of these consumes credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[0].note; controls[2].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin or skill > Users controls package user availability.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... Select the plugin that you want to manage. ... Open Users ... Managing a skill uses the same actions and steps as managing a plugin, so this section applies to both plugins and skills.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} can set availableTo to allowedForSome and allowedUsersAndGroups to user/group resource entities.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} ... availableTo ... Required if updating allowedUsersAndGroups. ... "resourceType": "user" ... "resourceType": "group" ... "availableTo": "allowedForSome"
claims.fix: In front matter and the rendered table, replace the call with 'PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}'. Add to the row note: 'The request body sets availableTo and allowedUsersAndGroups.' The cited reference supports the existing property names and values.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > skill > Block > Block blocks a standalone skill package.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block. ... Select Block, and then select Block again to confirm.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block prevents package usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: third row; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry lists plugin and separately packaged skill records.
claims.quote: Use Agents > Tools > Registry to review plugin and separately packaged skill records in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: GET /v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages?$filter=elementTypes/any(e:e eq 'AgentSkills') lists packages containing skills.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages ... To filter by element type, use the any lambda operator on the elementTypes collection ... AgentSkills | Titles that contain skills.

claims.claim: Build > skill > … > Share > Share is the complete maker route to skill sharing in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Open your agent in Copilot Studio. ... Select the Build tab. ... Select the skill you want to share to open the skill configuration panel. ... Select the three dots (…) and then select Share. ... On the details page, select Share in the upper-right corner.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Agents > agent > Build > skill > … > Share > Share'. The current route starts at a tab inside an agent without giving the way into that agent. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent in sources for its instruction 'Open the agent from the Agents page'; retain skills-manage as this control's docs link for the remaining steps.

claims.where: controls[3].api; controls[3].note; Governance controls: fourth row
claims.claim: No API for the maker-side shared-skill audience control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience "skill" "share" "API"; opened skills-manage and Package Management API update reference. The latter controls catalog packages, not this maker-side skill-sharing operation.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that these general package controls govern or inventory the Copilot Studio roadmap skills catalog.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog Microsoft 365 registry package governance harness data access; opened skills-manage, administrator-guide, manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and Package Management API overview. None identifies the roadmap catalog as these packages.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The package block control applies tenant-wide to a standalone skill package.
claims.quote: Block | Selected plugin package and its included agents, or selected standalone skill package. | Prevent users and agents from accessing the package. ... You can block a plugin or skill package across your entire organization

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: A bundled skill has no separate blocking control; its package's controls apply.
claims.quote: For a bundled skill, apply the plugin's controls. You can't block an individual skill inside a package today.

claims.claim: Package availability can be scoped to particular users and groups, including for standalone skills.
claims.quote: Manage user availability | Selected plugin or standalone skill package. | Make the package available to all users, no users, or specific users and groups.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components and connections.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components and connections.

claims.claim: Some skills, including those used in Word, Excel and PowerPoint, are stored in OneDrive rather than the plugin registry.
claims.quote: Don't assume every skill is stored in the plugin registry. Skills used in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive today.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access controls plugin access by Microsoft, organisational or certified external publisher category.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access. ... Under the installation settings, choose which publisher categories users can access: Microsoft, your organization, or certified external publishers.

claims.claim: The package update and block API operations are preview.
claims.quote: Update package (preview) | PATCH /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} ... Block (preview) | POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The Customer Conversation harness supports two skill types.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support two types of skills: Generative skills ... and Topic skills

claims.claim: The shared-skill page does not specify which harnesses Browse skills covers.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "skills" "sharing" "administrator" "harness"; opened skills-manage and skills-overview. The Browse skills section gives no explicit harness eligibility list.

claims.claim: Administrative roles specifically for the roadmap skills catalog are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles catalog; opened skills-manage, skills-overview and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers. No catalog-specific administrator role is stated.

claims.claim: The cited plugin-management page names AI Administrator and Global Administrator for MCP request approval, not as skills-management role requirements.
claims.quote: Review and approve MCP requests ... You must have access to the Tools page ... You must be able to grant tenant-wide consent. Two roles meet both requirements: AI Administrator. Global Administrator.
